subject: Pivota Labs — latency qualification & PoC plan (p95/p99, streaming, concurrency)
messages:
From: Alex Holt <alex.holt@pivota.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Desai <samir.desai@pivota.ai>, SRE Team <sre@pivota.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T14:12:00Z
Subject: Quick recap + latency targets we discussed

Hi Laura / team,

Thanks for the call today — good alignment overall. To make the PoC efficient, here are the concrete performance constraints we need you to validate in the hosted evaluation:  

- Targets (end-to-end, client -> Redwood -> model -> client): p95 < 180 ms, p99 < 380 ms for single-shot generative requests (no streams).
- Streaming: for streaming chat flows (token-by-token) we need median (50th) per-token delivery under 50 ms and p95 per-token under 120 ms for messages up to 512 tokens.
- Throughput / concurrency: typical sustained QPS is 220 req/s with bursts to 900 req/s for 10–30s; concurrency per client service expected ~60 concurrent connections.
- Payload shapes: avg prompt size ~1.6 KB, worst-case prompt ~12 KB. KV/cache sensitivity: we rely on prefix caching (many short prompts share prefixes).
- SLA concerns: if hosted cannot meet p99 targets under realistic burst patterns, we will need deterministic fallbacks to our legacy provider during degrade windows.

Attached sample traffic profile and a short trace excerpt. Can you confirm Redwood can run a PoC that exercises these shapes and propose a minimal test harness? Also please advise what telemetry/traces you need from our side (e.g., full tcp timestamps, client-level concurrency markers).

Next steps we expect from Redwood: test plan, required artifacts, timeline (2–3 week PoC preferred), and a clear gating decision matrix for accept/reject based on p95/p99 outcomes.

Thanks,
Alex
Head of Product, Pivota Labs

[attachment: pivota_traffic_profile.csv (CSV)]
[attachment: sample_trace.json (JSON)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Holt <alex.holt@pivota.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-18T18:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + latency targets we discussed

Hi Alex — great to talk, thanks for the clear list. Confirming receipt of the traffic profile and trace. High-level notes from our side:  

- Feasibility: the p95/p99 numbers you quoted are aggressive but realistic for our hosted runtime with the right configuration (small-batch sizing, prefix KV cache enabled, and routes pinned to low-latency instances). Streaming per-token targets are typically achievable; we will validate end-to-end including client reassembly time.
- Bursts: we can emulate your burst profile using our load harness; we’ll run mixed workloads (short vs long prompts) to capture amplification effects.
- Fallback: we support policy-based routing and can instrument automatic fallback to your legacy provider when cost/latency tradeoffs demand it; we’ll show how that behaves in the PoC.

Requested items from Pivota to run a concise PoC:
1) A short list of 8–10 representative prompt templates (we can synthesize traffic from them).
2) A daytime and nighttime baseline trace (you included a snippet; full trace for 24h preferred).
3) A contact in infra to coordinate TCP-level timestamps (for latency correlation).

Proposed PoC plan (2 weeks):
- Week 0 (this week): exchange artifacts + finalize test scenarios (we’ll draft a test plan by Tue 8/20).
- Week 1: hosted runs with increasing load, streaming and non-streaming runs, collect p95/p99, per-token metrics and token-delivery histograms.
- Week 2: mixed-burst stress, fallback exercises, shared analysis and decision meeting.

Ben and Rishi are looped on infra/test tooling. Ben — can you prepare a draft test plan and sample harness config by Monday? Rishi — we may want to instrument extra tracing hooks (span correlation id) for p99 attribution.

I’ll put a short PoC checklist into Drive and request a calendar for a decision review at the end of Week 2. If that works I’ll follow up with a calendar invite and a short DocuSign/POC statement so we can get an NDA/POC scoping in place quickly.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

[signature block]
[attachment: redwood_poc-checklist.pdf (PDF)]

From: Alex Holt <alex.holt@pivota.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Samir Desai <samir.desai@pivota.ai>, SRE Team <sre@pivota.ai>
Date: 2026-08-19T09:07:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + latency targets we discussed

Laura — thanks, that timeline looks good. A few clarifications:  

- Prompt templates: Samir will drop a short set (8 templates) into the Drive link below by EOD today.
- Traces: we can provide 6 hours of full tracing data for the busiest window (no PII) — will that be sufficient for p99 attribution? If you need 24h we can arrange it but it will take an extra day.
- Instrumentation: Samir (cc) is our infra lead; he can open a port to provide tcp-level timestamps or share exported traces (Zipkin/OTLP).

One operational ask: during the PoC, can Redwood expose a simple per-second CSV of observed p50/p95/p99 and a per-token latency histogram for streaming runs? That will help our SRE correlate client-side tails to server-side events.

Availability for decision review: Aug 31 — Sept 2 window works for our team.

Thanks — attaching the prompt templates short list to Drive.

—Alex

[link: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/pivota-poc-exchange]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Holt <alex.holt@pivota.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-08-20T10:45:00Z
Subject: Re: Quick recap + latency targets we discussed

Alex — perfect, appreciate the fast turn. Confirming next actions:  

1) Ben: draft test plan & harness config (due 2026-08-23).
2) Pivota: upload prompt templates + 6h trace (will accept; flag if you later send 24h).
3) Rishi: wire up span correlation id and CSV export for per-second P95/P99 (we’ll publish to the shared Drive).
4) Scheduling: I’ll book a 45-min decision review for Sept 1 at 16:00 ET (tentative) and share calendar once you confirm.

We’ll also include a short failure-mode doc that maps observed signal failures to decision gates (e.g., persistent p99 > threshold during bursts => fail, transient single-window spike => retry with cache tuning).

If Pivota can sign the standard PoC agreement we’ll schedule the dedicated run cluster. I’ll send the PoC statement (simple SOW-level doc) and DocuSign link by EOD.

Talk soon —
Laura
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
